correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact side-pair decomposition. Same-side double integral contributes 2Lt-mt²; each adjacent vertex maps a quadrant with Jacobian sin(theta) to a cone of opening pi-theta, contributing t²(pi-theta)/sin(theta) for both orientations. Positive small threshold eliminates all nonadjacent pairs and side truncation. Euler sine product gives h(x)=x/sin(x)=1+x²/6+positive even higher coefficients and h''(x)>1/3. Strict Jensen produces the quantitative extremum; tangential centrally symmetric m-gon angle perturbations establish 1/6 uniform sharpness. Executed python3 checker.py from the complete package: four independent corner-sector midpoint integrations; 250,000 boundary-pair trials on each of three convex polygons; 1,800 stability inequality vectors; five explicit high-side-count sharpness ratios. All checks passed and the final line was CHECKS_PASSED. The Monte Carlo checks have finite sampling error and are not used as universal proofs. Finite numerical evidence is not a proof.

value.rationale: The exact local chord-distance law is a natural geometric-probability statistic of boundary sampling. Its nontrivial coefficient is a local angular signature of corners, independent of side lengths. Sharp fixed-side-count shape ordering and equality classification, a quantitative angle-deviation bound, and its optimal universal factor provide meaningful structural information; this is not a numeric one-off or an arbitrary parameter slice. Unlike a routine finite computation, it is a complete theorem for every convex polygon with a global optimality construction.
